title: Français langue première - Grade 1 French Immersion
subject: Français langue première
description: A comprehensive French language arts program focusing on oral communication, reading, and writing development in an immersion context.
goals: Students will develop foundational French literacy skills through phonological awareness, sight word recognition, guided reading, and emergent writing.
themes: ["Ma famille et moi","Mon école","Les saisons et les fêtes","Les animaux","Ma communauté"]
overarchingQuestions: Comment puis-je communiquer mes idées en français? Comment les livres nous aident-ils à apprendre?
assessmentOverview: Ongoing observation, portfolio assessment, running records, and developmental writing samples.
resourceNeeds: Leveled French readers, alphabet resources, writing journals, phonics materials, French picture books
professionalGoals: Strengthen differentiated literacy instruction and incorporate more authentic French literature.
descriptionFr: Un programme complet d'arts langagiers axé sur la communication orale, la lecture et l'écriture en contexte d'immersion.
goalsFr: Les élèves développeront des compétences de base en littératie française par la conscience phonologique, la reconnaissance de mots fréquents, la lecture guidée et l'écriture émergente.
differentiationFramework: {"emergingLearners":"Heavy use of visual supports, gestures, and environmental print; partner support with stronger French speakers; simplified vocabulary and shorter phrases; multisensory learning through movement, music, and art","advancedLearners":"Extension activities with complex French texts; leadership opportunities helping classmates; creative projects requiring higher-order thinking in French; connections to French literature and culture beyond grade level","learningDifferences":"Assistive technology for French language access; alternative communication methods when needed; modified writing expectations with focus on meaning over mechanics; sensory supports for regulation during French instruction","englishLanguageLearners":"Explicit connection between home languages and French; visual vocabulary supports in multiple languages; recognition that multilingual learners have unique strengths; culturally responsive teaching acknowledging diverse backgrounds"}
thematicOverview: French language development through rich thematic units: September - Ma rentrée (Back to School) with classroom routines and greetings; October - Les couleurs de l'automne (Fall Colors) with seasonal vocabulary; November - Ma famille et moi (My Family and Me) exploring relationships; December - Les fêtes et traditions (Holidays and Traditions) with cultural celebrations; January - L'hiver magique (Magical Winter) with weather and activities; February - Les amis et l'amitié (Friends and Friendship) focusing on social connections; March - Le printemps arrive (Spring Arrives) with growth and change; April - Les animaux de notre monde (Animals of Our World) with nature exploration; May - Ma communauté (My Community) with local connections; June - Nos souvenirs et notre avenir (Our Memories and Future) reflecting on learning.
assessmentStrategy: {"oralCommunication":"Daily circle conversations, weekly Show and Tell in French, monthly oral storytelling assessments","reading":"Running records with French leveled readers, phonics assessments, sight word evaluations","writing":"Developmental writing portfolios, weekly journal entries, monthly thematic writing tasks","listening":"Response to French instructions and stories, comprehension activities with audio books","portfolio":"Student self-reflection using visual scales, parent conference evidence, celebration of growth"}
indigenousPerspectives: Authentic integration of Mi'kmaq perspectives throughout French learning: Mi'kmaq place names in Prince Edward Island pronounced and learned alongside French geographical terms; Traditional Mi'kmaq storytelling methods incorporated into French oral traditions, with Elders invited to share stories that connect to our French thematic units; Seasonal teachings aligned with Mi'kmaq understanding of natural cycles while building French vocabulary for weather, animals, and activities; Mi'kmaq family structures and community values explored when learning French family vocabulary, honoring diverse family configurations; Traditional Mi'kmaq games translated into French instruction, supporting physical activity and language learning.
resourceLibrary: {"literature":"French-Canadian picture books featuring diverse characters and PEI settings, traditional French fairy tales adapted for Grade 1, Indigenous stories available in French translation","digital":"French educational apps for phonics and vocabulary, virtual reality experiences of French-speaking communities, French children's songs and videos from Radio-Canada","manipulatives":"Magnetic French letters and sounds, French alphabet puzzles and cards, dramatic play props with French labels","authentic":"French food packages for environmental print, French maps and travel brochures, French children's magazines and newspapers"}
parentCommunication: {"weekly":"Français à la maison newsletter every Friday with phrases, activities, and celebrations","monthly":"Family French learning sessions where parents learn basic phrases and activities","homeConnection":"French phrase cards for family practice, suggestions for French cartoons and music","events":"Monthly Café français for families, invitations to French cultural performances"}

unitPlans.title: Welcome to School!
unitPlans.description: Introduction to French Immersion classroom, establishing routines, and building phonological awareness.
unitPlans.bigIdeas: We communicate through sounds and words. Our classroom is a French-speaking community.

**Sciences humaines**: Classroom community building, school mapping, understanding rules and routines

**Formation personnelle**: Identity exploration, emotional vocabulary in French, making friends

**Éducation physique**: Movement games with French instructions, body parts vocabulary

unitPlans.indigenousPerspectives: Mi'kmaq welcome protocols and greetings, importance of oral tradition.

unitPlans.socialJusticeConnections: Everyone's name is important, respecting different ways of saying hello.

thematicOverview: Mathematical thinking development through monthly thematic exploration: September - Collections de la classe (Classroom Collections) exploring sorting, counting, and early number concepts using classroom objects; October - Régularités d'automne (Fall Patterns) discovering patterns in nature, leaves, and seasonal changes while building number sequences; November - Nombres dans notre vie (Numbers in Our Life) investigating how we use numbers at home, school, and in our community; December - Formes et décorations (Shapes and Decorations) exploring 2D and 3D shapes through holiday decorations and winter geometry; January - Mesures et comparaisons (Measurement and Comparisons) using non-standard units to measure classroom objects and comparing lengths, weights; February - Problèmes et solutions (Problems and Solutions) developing problem-solving strategies through real-world mathematical challenges; March - Géométrie dans notre monde (Geometry in Our World) identifying shapes and spatial relationships in architecture and art; April - Données et graphiques (Data and Graphs) collecting, organizing, and representing information about weather, growth, and spring observations; May - Argent et achats (Money and Shopping) exploring Canadian coins and simple transactions; June - Révision mathématique (Mathematical Review) consolidating learning through games, investigations, and mathematical celebrations.

indigenousPerspectives: Respectful integration of Indigenous mathematical traditions: Traditional Mi'kmaq counting systems and number concepts shared alongside French numbers, with attention to cultural protocols and community guidance; Mi'kmaq seasonal calendar and natural patterns explored through mathematical observation and data collection; Traditional games involving mathematical thinking, such as bowl games and counting games, learned with cultural context and respect; Indigenous approaches to spatial reasoning and geometry through traditional art, beadwork patterns, and architectural designs; Mi'kmaq astronomical knowledge connecting to time, measurement, and cyclical thinking; Land-based mathematics learning from traditional ecological knowledge about animal populations, plant cycles, and resource management.

unitPlans.title: My Story Through Time
unitPlans.description: Organizing important life events in chronological order and understanding the concept of time and personal history.
unitPlans.bigIdeas: Everyone has a personal story. Events happen in order through time. We can remember and organize our memories.
unitPlans.essentialQuestions: ["Quelle est mon histoire personnelle?","Comment organiser les événements dans le temps?","Comment ai-je changé en grandissant?"]
unitPlans.descriptionFr: Organiser les événements importants de la vie en ordre chronologique et comprendre le concept du temps et de l'histoire personnelle.
unitPlans.bigIdeasFr: Chacun a une histoire personnelle. Les événements arrivent en ordre dans le temps. Nous pouvons nous souvenir et organiser nos souvenirs.

unitPlans.parentCommunicationPlan: Baby photo requests, family story sharing, memory artifact collection, growth measurement tracking.

unitPlans.title: Exploring Our World

unitPlans.bigIdeasFr: Nous pouvons trouver des lieux avec des cartes et des directions. Notre monde a plusieurs endroits spéciaux. Nous appartenons à différentes communautés.

unitPlans.successCriteria: ["Je peux créer de l'art pour célébrer","Je peux apprendre sur l'art de différentes cultures","Je peux faire de l'art à partager avec les autres"]

differentiationFramework: {"socialEmotionalChallenges":"Individualized behavior plans with positive reinforcement; additional support for emotional regulation and social skills","traumaExperiences":"Trauma-informed approaches to social-emotional learning; recognition of individual triggers and support needs","autismDifferences":"Visual supports and structured social learning opportunities; explicit teaching of social norms and expectations","englishLanguageLearners":"Social-emotional learning that transcends language barriers; peer support and buddy systems","anxietyNeeds":"Modified expectations for social participation; additional supports for emotional regulation"}
thematicOverview: Social-emotional learning integrated throughout daily experiences: September - Se connaître soi-même (Getting to Know Myself) exploring personal identity, strengths, and uniqueness; October - Émotions et sentiments (Emotions and Feelings) developing emotional vocabulary and regulation strategies; November - Relations familiales (Family Relationships) appreciating family diversity and building family connections; December - Gratitude et générosité (Gratitude and Generosity) developing appreciation and giving spirit during holiday season; January - Objectifs et résolutions (Goals and Resolutions) setting personal goals and developing growth mindset; February - Amitié et empathie (Friendship and Empathy) building social skills and understanding others' perspectives; March - Sécurité et bien-être (Safety and Wellness) learning personal safety and wellness strategies; April - Résolution de conflits (Conflict Resolution) developing peaceful problem-solving skills; May - Responsabilité et leadership (Responsibility and Leadership) exploring personal and community responsibility; June - Croissance et avenir (Growth and Future) reflecting on personal development and planning ahead.

indigenousPerspectives: Seven Sacred Teachings integrated into character development: WISDOM (Nibwaakaawin) - Cherishing knowledge and understanding, seeking guidance from Elders and teachers, appreciating traditional knowledge alongside contemporary learning. LOVE (Zaagi'idiwin) - Developing unconditional love for family, community, and all living things; showing care and compassion in daily interactions. RESPECT (Mnaadendimowin) - Honoring all people, cultures, and living beings; showing respect for differences and diverse ways of being; respecting traditional territories and cultural protocols. TRUTH (Debwewin) - Being honest in words and actions; understanding the importance of truthfulness in relationships; speaking and living authentically. HUMILITY (Dibaadendizwin) - Recognizing individual place in the larger community; appreciating others' gifts and contributions; understanding interconnectedness with all life.
